title: Stalk of a finite direct image of an etale sheaf of sets
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $H$ a sheaf of sets on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], with direct image $f_*H$, $(f_*H)(V)=H(V\times_YX)$ for $V$ in $Y_{\Et}$, and $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $P(\bar y)$ be the set of geometric points $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $f\circ\bar x=\bar y$. For $\bar x\in P(\bar y)$ let $r_{\bar x}:(f_*H)_{\bar y}\to H_{\bar x}$ (stalks of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]) send the germ at a pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar y$ of $s\in(f_*H)(V)=H(V\times_YX)$ to the germ of $s$ at the pointed etale neighbourhood $(V\times_YX,(\bar v,\bar x))$ of $\bar x$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $P(\bar y)$ is finite and the map
$$(r_{\bar x})_{\bar x\in P(\bar y)}:(f_*H)_{\bar y}\longrightarrow\prod_{\bar x\in P(\bar y)}H_{\bar x}$$
is bijective.

proof.text: *The strict henselization at $\bar y$ and its geometric point.* Let $y\in Y$ be the image of $\bar y$ and $\kappa(\bar y)\subset\Omega$ the separable algebraic closure of $\kappa(y)$ in $\Omega$. Put $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}=\varinjlim A_V$ over the affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V,\bar v)$ of $\bar y$, $Y^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Spec}C$, with $c_V:Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\to V$ and $q:Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\to Y$ as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] (1) (for the scheme $Y$ and $\bar x=\bar y$): $C$ is a strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], whose maximal ideal we write $\mathfrak m_C$; its residue field is identified with $\kappa(\bar y)$, which is separably closed; and, writing $\bar y^{\mathrm{sh}}:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\bar y)\to Y^{\mathrm{sh}}$ (inclusion $\kappa(\bar y)\subset\Omega$, then the closed point), $c_V\circ\bar y^{\mathrm{sh}}=\bar v$ for every affine $(V,\bar v)$ and $q\circ\bar y^{\mathrm{sh}}=\bar y$. As a ring map, $\bar y^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is $\chi_0:C\to C/\mathfrak m_C\cong\kappa(\bar y)\subset\Omega$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; we regard $\Omega$ as a $C$-algebra through $\chi_0$. Let $X^{\mathrm{sh}}=Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\times_YX$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $f^{\mathrm{sh}}:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to Y^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $p:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to X$, and let $G=p^{-1}H$, a sheaf of sets on $X^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units].

proof.text: *The stalk is the set of sections over $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ (Stacks: 'By Theorem 03Q9 the stalk ... is computed by $H^q(X^{sh}_{\bar y},\mathcal F)$', here $q=0$, sheaves of sets).* A finite morphism is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. So [lem-weil-pbc-sets-pushforward-stalk-strict-henselization] applies to $f$, $H$, $\bar y$ (with the objects $C,Y^{\mathrm{sh}},c_V,q,X^{\mathrm{sh}},f^{\mathrm{sh}},p$ of step 1): every element of $(f_*H)_{\bar y}$ is the germ at an affine pointed etale neighbourhood, and the map $\Theta:(f_*H)_{\bar y}\to G(X^{\mathrm{sh}})$, $\Theta(\text{germ of }s\text{ at }(V,\bar v))=G(\sigma_V)(p^*s)$, with $\sigma_V=((c_V\circ f^{\mathrm{sh}},p),\mathrm{id}):X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to(V\times_YX)\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}}$, is bijective.

proof.text: *$X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the spectrum of a finite $C$-algebra (Stacks: 'Since $f$ is finite, $X^{sh}_{\bar y}$ is finite over $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O^{sh}_{Y,\bar y})$, thus $X^{sh}_{\bar y}=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$').* By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a) the base change $f^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of the finite $f$ is finite, and by (b), $Y^{\mathrm{sh}}$ being affine, $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is affine; write $X^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $f^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta)$ for a ring map $\beta:C\to B$. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] (for the affine open $Y^{\mathrm{sh}}$ itself, with inverse image $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$) $B$ is a finitely generated $C$-module.

source.place: Proposition Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), proof: 'Since f is finite, X^sh_ybar is finite over Spec(O^sh_{Y,ybar}), thus X^sh_ybar = Spec(A) for some ring A finite over O^sh_{Y,ybar}'

proof.text: *$B$ is a finite product of strictly henselian local rings (Stacks: 'Lemma 04GH implies that $A$ is a finite product of henselian local rings $A=A_1\times\dots\times A_r$. Since the residue field of $\mathcal O^{sh}_{Y,\bar y}$ is separably closed the same is true for each $A_i$. Hence $A_i$ is strictly henselian').* $C$ is henselian (step 1), so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] there are $r\ge0$ and an isomorphism of $C$-algebras $B\cong B_1\times\dots\times B_r$ with each $(B_i,\mathfrak n_i)$ a henselian local ring, finite as a $C$-module, $C\to B_i$ local, and $\kappa_i=B_i/\mathfrak n_i$ a finite field extension of $C/\mathfrak m_C\cong\kappa(\bar y)$. Since $\kappa(\bar y)$ is separably closed (step 1), $\kappa_i$ is separably closed by [lem-weil-pbc-sepclosed-finite-extension-unique-embedding] (a); so each $B_i$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

source.place: Proposition Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), proof: 'Lemma 04GH implies ... Hence A_i is strictly henselian'

proof.text: *The pieces (Stacks: 'This implies that $X^{sh}_{\bar y}=\coprod_{i=1}^r\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$').* Let $e_i\in B$ be the idempotent corresponding to $(0,\dots,1,\dots,0)$ (the $1$ in place $i$); $e_ie_j=0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\sum_ie_i=1$. Put $U_i=D(e_i)\subseteq X^{\mathrm{sh}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] each $U_i$ is open and closed; the $U_i$ are pairwise disjoint (a prime containing neither $e_i$ nor $e_j$ would not contain $e_ie_j=0$) and cover $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ (a prime containing all $e_i$ contains $\sum e_i=1$). The principal open $U_i=D(e_i)$ is the open subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}B[1/e_i]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $B[1/e_i]\cong B_i$ (the projection $B\to B_i$ sends $e_i$ to $1$ and has kernel $(1-e_i)B$, and $e_i(1-e_i)=0$). So $U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, with $B_i$ strictly henselian local (step 4); let $u_i\in U_i$ be its closed point (the prime of $B$ that is the preimage of $\mathfrak n_i$). If $r=0$ then $B=0$ and $X^{\mathrm{sh}}=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), proof: 'This implies that X^sh_ybar = coprod_{i=1}^r Spec(A_i)'

proof.text: *The geometric points over $\bar y$ (the index set of the product in 03QP (1)).* (a) Let $P^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the set of $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ with $f^{\mathrm{sh}}\circ\bar t=\bar y^{\mathrm{sh}}$. For $\bar x\in P(\bar y)$, $f\circ\bar x=\bar y=q\circ\bar y^{\mathrm{sh}}$ (step 1), so $\bar x^{\mathrm{sh}}=(\bar y^{\mathrm{sh}},\bar x)$ is defined [def-pc-fibre-product] and lies in $P^{\mathrm{sh}}$; conversely for $\bar t\in P^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $f\circ p\circ\bar t=q\circ f^{\mathrm{sh}}\circ\bar t=q\circ\bar y^{\mathrm{sh}}=\bar y$, so $p\circ\bar t\in P(\bar y)$, and $\bar t=(f^{\mathrm{sh}}\bar t,p\bar t)=(p\circ\bar t)^{\mathrm{sh}}$. So $\bar x\mapsto\bar x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is a bijection $P(\bar y)\to P^{\mathrm{sh}}$ with inverse $\bar t\mapsto p\circ\bar t$. (b) By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the elements of $P^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are the $C$-algebra maps $\chi:B\to\Omega$ ($\Omega$ a $C$-algebra through $\chi_0$, step 1). For such $\chi$ the $\chi(e_i)$ are idempotents of the field $\Omega$, pairwise orthogonal with sum $1$, so exactly one $i$ has $\chi(e_i)=1$ and $\chi$ kills $(1-e_i)B$: $\chi$ factors through a $C$-algebra map $\chi_i:B_i\to\Omega$. Its image is a domain which is a finite-dimensional vector space over the field $\chi_0(C)$, hence a field, so $\ker\chi_i$ is a maximal ideal of the local ring $B_i$, i.e. $\ker\chi_i=\mathfrak n_i$, and $\chi_i$ induces a field homomorphism $\kappa_i\to\Omega$ extending $C/\mathfrak m_C\cong\kappa(\bar y)\subset\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sepclosed-finite-extension-unique-embedding] (with $K=\kappa(\bar y)$, separably closed by step 1, $L=\kappa_i$ finite over $K$ by step 4, and $\iota$ the inclusion into $\Omega$) (b) there is exactly one such field homomorphism $\lambda_i:\kappa_i\to\Omega$. Conversely $B\to B_i\to\kappa_i\xrightarrow{\lambda_i}\Omega$ is a $C$-algebra map. Hence $P^{\mathrm{sh}}=\{\bar t_1,\dots,\bar t_r\}$ with $\bar t_i$ the geometric point given by $B\to B_i\to\kappa_i\xrightarrow{\lambda_i}\Omega$, these are pairwise distinct, and the image of $\bar t_i$ is the point $u_i$ of step 5. With (a): $P(\bar y)=\{\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_r\}$, $\bar x_i=p\circ\bar t_i$, pairwise distinct, so $P(\bar y)$ is finite and $i\mapsto\bar x_i$ is a bijection $\{1,\dots,r\}\to P(\bar y)$ with $\bar x_i^{\mathrm{sh}}=\bar t_i$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), proof and statement (1): the index set '{xbar : Spec(k) -> X, f(xbar) = ybar}' of the product, matched with the factors A_i

proof.text: *Sections over $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are the product of the sections over the pieces.* The open immersions $U_i\to X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and jointly surjective (step 5), so $\{U_i\to X^{\mathrm{sh}}\}_{i=1}^r$ is a covering in $X^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] $U_i\times_{X^{\mathrm{sh}}}U_j$ is the open subscheme $U_i\cap U_j$ with both projections the inclusions: it is empty for $i\ne j$, and $U_i$ with both projections $\mathrm{id}$ for $i=j$. The empty family is a covering of the empty scheme $\varnothing$ (an object of $X^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\Et}$), so the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] makes $G(\varnothing)\to\prod_{\varnothing}=\{*\}$ bijective: $G(\varnothing)$ has one element. Hence in the sheaf condition for $\{U_i\to X^{\mathrm{sh}}\}$ the two maps to $\prod_{i,j}G(U_i\times U_j)$ agree on every family (components $i\ne j$ lie in the one-point set $G(\varnothing)$, components $i=j$ are both $s_i$), so $\rho:G(X^{\mathrm{sh}})\to\prod_{i=1}^rG(U_i)$, $a\mapsto(a|_{U_i})_i$, is bijective. (For $r=0$ this is again $G(\varnothing)=\{*\}$.)

source.place: Proposition Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), proof: sections over X^sh_ybar = coprod Spec(A_i) are the product of the sections over the Spec(A_i)

proof.text: *Each piece computes a stalk (Stacks: 'Part (1) follows from the corresponding statement of Lemma 03QO').* For each $i$, $U_i\subseteq X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is an open subscheme isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with $B_i$ strictly henselian local (steps 4, 5), and $\bar t_i$ is a geometric point of $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ whose image is the closed point $u_i$ of $U_i$ (step 6). By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-strictly-henselian-open-sections-stalk] (with $T=X^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $U=U_i$, $\bar t=\bar t_i$) the germ map $g_i:G(U_i)\to G_{\bar t_i}$ at $(U_i,\bar t_i)$ is bijective.

source.place: Proposition Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), proof: 'Part (1) follows from the corresponding statement of Lemma 03QO'

proof.text: *Stalks of the inverse image.* By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ] (with $e=p$, $T=X^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $S=X$, $\bar t=\bar t_i$, so $\bar s=p\circ\bar t_i=\bar x_i$) there is a bijection $c_i:G_{\bar t_i}=(p^{-1}H)_{\bar t_i}\to H_{\bar x_i}$ with $c_i(\text{germ of }p^*a\text{ at }(W\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}},(\bar w,\bar t_i)))=\text{germ of }a\text{ at }(W,\bar w)$ for every pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar x_i$ and $a\in H(W)$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), proof: the identification (F|_{X^sh})_{xbar^sh} = F_xbar, Lemma Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback) for sheaves of sets

proof.text: *The composite is $(r_{\bar x})_{\bar x}$; conclusion.* Let $\Phi:(f_*H)_{\bar y}\to\prod_{i=1}^rH_{\bar x_i}$ be the composite of $\Theta$ (step 2), $\rho$ (step 7), $\prod_ig_i$ (step 8) and $\prod_ic_i$ (step 9); it is bijective. Let $\alpha\in(f_*H)_{\bar y}$; by step 2 $\alpha$ is the germ at an affine $(V,\bar v)$ of some $s\in(f_*H)(V)=H(V\times_YX)$. Put $W=V\times_YX$, an object of $X_{\Et}$, and $\theta=G(\sigma_V)(p^*s)=\Theta(\alpha)$. The germ is unchanged by restriction along a morphism of pointed etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: the inclusion $(U_i,\bar t_i)\to(X^{\mathrm{sh}},\bar t_i)$ and $\sigma_V:(X^{\mathrm{sh}},\bar t_i)\to(W\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}},\sigma_V\circ\bar t_i)$ are such morphisms, so $g_i(\theta|_{U_i})$ is the germ of $p^*s$ at $(W\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}},\sigma_V\circ\bar t_i)$. Now [def-pc-fibre-product] $\sigma_V\circ\bar t_i=((c_V\circ f^{\mathrm{sh}}\circ\bar t_i,p\circ\bar t_i),\bar t_i)=((c_V\circ\bar y^{\mathrm{sh}},\bar x_i),\bar t_i)=((\bar v,\bar x_i),\bar t_i)$ by steps 1 and 6. By step 9 (with the pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,(\bar v,\bar x_i))$ of $\bar x_i$ and $a=s$), $c_i(g_i(\theta|_{U_i}))$ is the germ of $s$ at $(V\times_YX,(\bar v,\bar x_i))$, which is $r_{\bar x_i}(\alpha)$ by the definition of $r_{\bar x_i}$ in the statement. Hence $\Phi=(r_{\bar x_i})_{i=1}^r$. Since $i\mapsto\bar x_i$ is a bijection $\{1,\dots,r\}\to P(\bar y)$ (step 6), $P(\bar y)$ is finite and $(r_{\bar x})_{\bar x\in P(\bar y)}:(f_*H)_{\bar y}\to\prod_{\bar x\in P(\bar y)}H_{\bar x}$ is $\Phi$ up to this reindexing, hence bijective.
